onboarding.welcomeSubtitle: Securely watch a computer from a distance — or let someone watch yours. We'll set this computer up. You only need to do this once.
onboarding.roleQuestion: What will you use this computer for?
onboarding.roleHint: Pick what fits. You can choose both.
onboarding.hostTitle: I want to get help on this computer
onboarding.hostSubtitle: Someone else can then watch this screen — but only when you click “Yes” at that moment. Choose this if you want to be helped.
onboarding.clientTitle: I want to help someone else
onboarding.clientSubtitle: You watch someone else's computer to help them. Choose this if you're the one helping.
onboarding.changeLater: You can always change this later.
onboarding.serverSubtitle: A server connects you over the internet or to managed devices. You usually get its address from your administrator. You can skip this and add one later under Servers — or connect directly on your local network.
onboarding.nameHint: A name you recognise, for example “Work”.
onboarding.serverHint: The web address of the server. The app takes care of the rest.
onboarding.deviceSubtitle: This is how others see which computer is yours.

connect.signInSubtitle: Sign in to see the computers in your organisation.
connect.noDevices: No computers in your organisation yet.
connect.consoleInputHint: For an authorized Ubuntu console, click the screen or type while it is focused.
connect.requestingSession: Requesting a session — the host may ask for approval…
connect.sessionCodeSubtitle: Ad-hoc support without an account — the host shares a code.
connect.sessionCodeNote: This connection method is still being built (server + protocol).
connect.lanSubtitle: Connect directly to another computer nearby — no server needed.
connect.lanNoneFound: No computers found yet. Make sure the other computer is sharing on this network, then search again.
connect.lanPinLabel: PIN (if the other computer shows one)
connect.lanPinHint: Leave empty to connect with this device's key instead.
connect.errUnreachable: Can't reach that computer. It's probably not sharing anymore, or it's switched off.
connect.errTimeout: The connection timed out. Is the other computer still sharing on this network?
connect.errAuth: The connection was refused. Is the code correct?
connect.errNotTrusted: This device isn't allowed yet. Enter the code, or ask the other computer to allow it under Access.
connect.errNoRoute: This computer is not available on your local network and no matching relay connection is ready. If it is an Ubuntu physical console, enable its physical-console service first.

device.identitySubtitle: Give this key to a support client so they can trust it in advance (TOFU).
device.receiveHelpIntro: This screen is reachable on the local network whenever the app is open — no server needed. Read out your computer name and code to let someone connect.
device.unavailable: Sharing isn't available on this device yet.
device.waitingTitle: Waiting for a helper to connect…
device.waitingHint: Tell the helper your computer name and this code. They pick you under “Local network” and enter the code.
device.shareAllHint: Off limits the helper to your main screen. On lets them switch between all your screens.
device.rememberHint: Then it can connect without the code next time. Key:
device.helperRemembered: This helper is remembered and can join without the code.

relays.name: Name
relays.serverHint: The app creates the secure connection itself.

settings.name: Name
settings.privateNote: The private key never leaves this device.
settings.startupToggle: Start RivetLink when I log in
settings.startupHint: Recommended for a device that should always be reachable, like a computer at home you connect back to.

headless.title: Ubuntu headless host
headless.intro: Set up this Ubuntu computer for secure, monitorless screenshots after a reboot. Choose Local network when both devices are at home on the same network.
headless.configuredHint: This computer captures only its dedicated virtual monitor. The relay never sees the screen unencrypted.
headless.dialogTitle: Set up a headless Ubuntu host
headless.warning: This makes system changes: RivetLink installs the GNOME/PipeWire requirements and two non-root user services. Ubuntu will ask you to approve this with your system password.
headless.scope: Only the RivetLink client on this device is pre-trusted. RivetLink uses your current signed-in session to register this Home Node securely, so you never need to copy a token. That client can request on-demand encrypted screenshots; it cannot control input, open a shell, access files, or stream live video.
headless.localNetworkHint: No server or account is needed. RivetLink discovers this Home Node on your local network; only this pre-trusted app can request screenshots.
headless.relayHint: Requires a selected relay and a signed-in session. Use this to connect when away from your local network.
headless.name: Name for this Home Node
headless.controllerKey: Public key of your controller device
headless.controllerKeyHint: On your laptop/phone, open RivetLink → Settings → Security and copy the public key. Only that device is allowed.
headless.removeWarning: This stops the two RivetLink user services and removes the local headless identity, keys, and configuration.
headless.removeBody: GNOME/PipeWire packages, this app's saved allowed devices, and any relay-side device record remain. You can then set up this host again.

physicalConsole.title: Ubuntu physical console
physicalConsole.intro: Configure this Ubuntu computer for unattended access through the real GDM login screen and a permanently connected HDMI dummy.
physicalConsole.configuredHint: The non-root RivetLink broker starts at boot and uses the real GDM/GNOME display, not a virtual desktop.
physicalConsole.warning: This installs a restricted non-root system service and a GDM/GNOME session worker. An HDMI dummy must remain connected. Ubuntu asks once for your system password.
physicalConsole.scope: Paste the public key of the separate laptop or desktop that will control this Ubuntu computer. That device is explicitly trusted for encrypted display and pointer/keyboard input at GDM or your own session. RivetLink never stores or reads your Ubuntu password; type it only in the remote GDM window. There is no shell, file access, clipboard or Ubuntu automatic login.
physicalConsole.localNetworkHint: Direct encrypted access on this LAN. No relay, account or internet connection is required for this route.
physicalConsole.relayHint: Encrypted remote access outside this network. Requires a selected relay and signed-in session only when enabled.
physicalConsole.name: Name for this Ubuntu Home Node
physicalConsole.controllerKeyHint: On the separate controlling laptop/desktop, open RivetLink → Settings → Security and copy its public key. Do not use this Ubuntu computer's own key.

access.keyHint: The other device shows this under Settings → Identity.
access.osPasswordHint: Confirms it's really you changing who can access this device.
